entries.name: Del Greenblatt

expected.sentence: Arrested 1961-06-09. The Civil Rights Digital Library establishes the arrest and the identification photograph but not the disposition, any transfer to Parchman, or the release date — unresolved pending court, jail, or penitentiary records.

entries.name: Robertson Wood

expected.charges: Detained during Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party voting-rights demonstrations; individual charge unverified
expected.sentence: Ten days actually detained at the Mississippi state fairgrounds in Jackson; released June 24, 1965. Formal sentence unverified.

entries.rationale: July6,1965 Canadian Friends of SNCC newsletter p1 reports June24 release after10days; Wood firsthand account specifies June14–24 detention period. Original visually verified.

entries.name: Jim Wilson

expected.charges: Refusal of military induction — Newark federal prosecution, 1966
expected.sentence:
Sentenced in Newark on December 9, 1966 to three years in prison. Actual time served and release date remain unverified.

Sources: https://merton.bellarmine.edu/files/original/0482e764eec85f6fec19cbf76b331818b359fb5e.pdf

updates.sentence:
Sentenced in Newark on December 9, 1966 to three years in prison. Dorothy Day reported in December 1968 that he had left Allenwood after 22 months in prison. Exact custody endpoints remain unverified.

Sources: https://merton.bellarmine.edu/files/original/0482e764eec85f6fec19cbf76b331818b359fb5e.pdf

entries.rationale: Dorothy Day explicitly reports actual22months after release. Separate suspended draft-card sentence untouched.

entries.name: Victor Richman

expected.charges: Knowingly violating a Coast Guard restricted-zone order at the Ethan Allen launching; 50 U.S.C. 192.
expected.prosecutor: John P. Diuguid; Hadley W. Austin
expected.sentence: One year, with 90 days to serve and the balance suspended. He remained in New Haven custody several days after the November 22, 1960 arrest. An August 1961 report describes his confinement at Danbury, including four days in solitary before a fast. His complete custody span and final release date are unverified.

entries.rationale: Contemporary AP Nov23 reports all nine including Richman jailed after Nov22 launch action. Nov26 AP original corroborates continued NewHaven custody. No fullsentence counted as actualtime.

entries.name: Craig W. Anderson

expected.charges: Desertion from the USS Intrepid after refusing to return from shore leave in Japan as a protest against the Vietnam War.
expected.sentence: Remained outside U.S. military jurisdiction; traveled through the Soviet Union and entered exile in Sweden.

updates.sentence: Returned to the United States in 1971 after exile in Sweden. Arrested by the FBI in San Francisco March 30, 1972; spent eight months in jail before receiving three years of probation and a dishonorable discharge, according to the March 10, 1981 UPI report. Exact physical release date remains unresolved.

entries.rationale: UPI original p2B/PDF6 visually verifies March30,1972 and8actualmonths. Return described as year after1970; use1971YEAR. Correct earlier1967Swedenarrival used as exileend. Same desertion case expanded with ensuing custody, no duplicate case created.
